glosses: heading; header; title; headline; caption
название книги, статьи, раздела в тексте
полигр. строка, содержащая такое название и оформленная особым образом для выделения и привлечения внимания
The name of a film, musical piece, painting, or other work of art.

examples.text: I know the singer's name, but not the title of the song.

glosses: The name of a writing such as a book, which identifies it and usually describes its subject, with a short phrase that often summarizes its topic.
A published piece of media.

examples.text: The retailer carries thousands of titles.
Buyers of the new video game console can choose from three bundled titles.

glosses: A section or division of a writing, as of an act of law or a book.

examples.text: Title II of the USA PATRIOT Act

glosses: An appellation given to a person or family to signify either veneration, official position, social rank, the possession of assets or properties, or a professional or academic qualification; a style. (For examples, see :Category:en:Titles.)

examples.text:
Our bosom interest: go pronounce his present death
With his former title greet Macbeth.

The old man had always favored the match. He liked Clayton, and, being of an old southern family, he put rather an exaggerated value on the advantages of a title, which meant little or nothing to his daughter.
He read the letter aloud. Sophia listened with the studied air of one for whom, even in these days, a title possessed some surreptitious allurement.

glosses: Legal right to ownership of a property; a deed or other certificate proving this.

examples.text: a good title to an estate, or an imperfect title

glosses: In canon law, that by which a beneficiary holds a benefice.
A church to which a priest was ordained, and where he was to reside.
A written title, credit, or caption shown with a film, video, or performance.

examples.text: The titles scrolled by too quickly to read.

glosses: The recognition given to the winner of a championship in sports.
The panel for the name, between the bands of the back of a book.

examples.text: With some City fans already leaving the stadium in tears, Edin Dzeko equalised in the second of five minutes of stoppage time before Sergio Aguero scored the goal that won the title.

Equally disadvantageous to Jackson was the fact that other than the Jacksonville Athletic Club and the National Sporting Club, virtually no organization was willing to sponsor a title fight between a black fighter and a white one.

glosses: A long title.
A short title.
To assign a title to; to entitle.
The heading or title of a magazine or newspaper article.

examples.text: The headline on today's newspaper reads "John Doe Wins Wood-Splitting Competition."

Say that you'll never, never, never, never need it
One headline, why believe it?
Everybody wants to rule the world

Risk is everywhere. From tabloid headlines insisting that coffee causes cancer (yesterday, of course, it cured it) to stern government warnings about alcohol and driving, the world is teeming with goblins. For each one there is a frighteningly precise measurement of just how likely it is to jump from the shadows and get you.

glosses: The line at the top of a page containing the folio or number of the page.
The top-billed attraction.
A headrope.
To give a headline to a page or section of a text.

examples.text: Once again I take typewriter in hand to express my opinion on two very different issues. Good luck in deciding what to headline this letter.

glosses: To present as the main attraction; to have top billing, to be the main attraction.
Frase o palabra con que se enuncia el asunto o nombre de una obra, o alguna de sus partes o capítulos.

examples.text: ¿Por qué creen que Gabriel García Márquez puso como título «Cien años de soledad» a su novela?

glosses: Nombre de una obra artística en general.

examples.text: Sí, el título es «Damián»; y lo consigues en cualquier librería.

glosses: Distintivo con el que se le conoce a alguien, ya sea por sus cualidades o acciones.

examples.text: Cleopatra tenía el título de «la boca de los diez mil hombres.

glosses: Dícese de alguna dignidad nobiliaria o de la persona que la posee.
Honor o distinción que alguien logra conseguir, especialmente en algún concurso o campeonato.
Razón, causa, motivo o pretexto.

examples.text: No tener título para excusarse.

glosses: Dícese de cada una de las partes principales en las que se dividen y subdividen las leyes y reglamentos.
Instrumento o testimonio dado para desempeñar un empleo o profesión.
Instrumento legal que explica o legitima la posesión o transmisión de un derecho real.
Acto por el que se transmite un derecho real.
Documento que refrenda tal acto.
En particular, documento que refrenda un crédito contra otra persona o entidad, o la posesión de acciones.
Honor o distinción concedida al vencedor en un campeonato o competencia deportiva.

examples.text: Gané ese título después de vencer al equipo contrario en un campeonato de vóleibol.

glosses: Cuantificación de la proporción de una solución.
Acción de encabezar o empadronar.
Registro, matrícula o padrón que se hace de las personas o vecinos para la imposición de los tributos.
Ajuste de la suma o cuota que deben pagar los vecinos por toda la contribución, ya sea en diferentes ramos o ya en uno solo.

Conjunto de las palabras con que, según fórmula, se empieza un testamento, un memorial, una ejecutoria, etcétera, y también lo que, como advertencia o en otro concepto, se dice al principio de un libro o escrito de cualquier clase.
Texte écrit en haut d’une lettre, d’une brochure, d’un document, etc.

examples.text: Papier à en-tête.
Faire imprimer des en-têtes de lettres.
En amenant à soi une feuille de papier à en-tête administratif, il y jeta ces lignes de sa large écriture.

glosses: Variante orthographique de en-tête.

examples.text: À l’intérieur, il y avait plusieurs feuilles à entête de la clinique.
